rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for a discoloured mark left by a spill or contact with a substance.

example.english: There’s a coffee stain on the cuff of this shirt, and it won’t come out no matter how I wash it.
example.traditional: 件衫袖口有咖啡污漬，點洗都洗唔甩。
example.jyutping: gin6 saam1 zau6 hau2 jau5 gaa3 fe1 wu1 zik1 dim2 sai2 dou1 sai2 m4 lat1

rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose colloquial verb when a substance makes something dirty or stained.

example.english: Spilling soy sauce can stain the table.
example.traditional: 豉油一倒落張枱，就整污糟張枱喇。
example.jyutping: si6 jau4 jat1 dou2 lok6 zoeng1 ci5 zau6 zing2 wu1 zou1 zoeng1 ci5 laa3

rows.note: Use this for damaging or smearing a person's character, reputation, or good name.

example.english: Someone is badmouthing me around the office to stain my reputation.
example.traditional: 有人喺公司周圍唱衰我，想抹黑我嘅名聲。
example.jyutping: jau5 jan4 hai2 gung1 si1 zau1 wai4 coeng3 seoi1 ngo5 soeng2 mut3 hak1 ngo5 ge3 ming4 sing1

rows.note: Use this for a blemish on someone’s character, record, or reputation rather than a physical mark.

example.english: That scandal became a permanent stain on his career.
example.traditional: 呢宗醜聞成為佢事業上永遠嘅污點。
example.jyutping: ne1 zung1 cau2 man4 sing4 wai4 keoi5 si6 jip6 soeng6 wing5 jyun5 ge3 wu1 dim2

rows.note: Use this predicatively, usually with 咗, when an object has become dirty or stained rather than when someone deliberately stains it.

example.english: The white shirt got a stain from curry sauce.
example.traditional: 件白恤衫畀咖喱汁整到污糟咗。
example.jyutping: gin6 baak6 seot1 saam1 bei2 gaa3 lei1 zap1 zing2 dou3 wu1 zou1 zo2

rows.note: Use this in a wood-finishing or surface-colouring context for a substance absorbed into the material to colour it.

example.english: This wood stain soaks into the grain and gives it a much more natural colour.
example.traditional: 呢種木器染料會滲入木紋，令個色自然好多。
example.jyutping: ne1 zung2 muk6 hei3 jim5 liu2 wui5 sam3 jap6 muk6 man4 ling6 go3 sik1 zi6 jin4 hou2 do1
